solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Distressed husband inquires about Liberal surrender (10)

indicators.note: something distressed has been knocked about and damaged, so its letters are out of shape
the husband and inquires go round the Liberal, so L joins the mix of letters

annotation.surface: A worried husband asks whether a Liberal politician is about to give up.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to read inquires as a verb; it is only a bag of letters for the mix.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both words mean to give something up or hand it over.

entries.clue: Express first to run article on slump being over (5)

indicators.note: the first of the word run is its opening letter
something over has been turned over, and in a down clue that sends the word upwards

blocks.note: a dip = a slump, here written upwards

annotation.surface: A market report: an express train running into a slump.
annotation.walkthrough: Express looks like a verb or a train; it is the adjective, as in express delivery.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: an express train or delivery is a fast one.

entries.clue: Reconstruction of US–Italian boat that sank (9)

indicators.note: reconstructing something rebuilds it in a new form, so the letters come out in a new order

annotation.surface: A joint US–Italian project to rebuild a famous wreck.
annotation.walkthrough: The Lusitania was the British liner torpedoed in 1915 with many Americans aboard, so the US link is apt.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the Cunard liner sunk by a U-boat off Ireland in 1915.

entries.clue: Press here for further information? (4,10)

blocks.note: the surface pushes a button to push; the setter means the press, journalists, gathered here
not a help link but reporters there to get more facts

annotation.surface: An instruction on a web page or device: press this button to learn more.
annotation.walkthrough: Press is the gathered journalists, not a button, and they are here to extract further information.
annotation.definitionFit: Journalists, collectively the press, gather at such an event to be told more.

entries.clue: State of university weightlifter announced (7)

indicators.note: something announced is said out loud, so we want the sound of the word

annotation.surface: A national team's student weightlifter being named.
annotation.walkthrough: The weightlifter is a machine, not an athlete.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an Eastern European country is a state.

entries.clue: Hidden meaning of message from Times staffer? (7)

annotation.surface: Reading between the lines of a note from someone at The Times.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a sub is just one example of a Times staffer; this puzzle is in The Times.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: what lies beneath the literal words of a text is its hidden meaning.

entries.clue: City’s first to abandon support for Bank of Scotland (4)

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it, so the C leaves the word

annotation.surface: The City of London withdrawing support for the Bank of Scotland in a crisis.
annotation.walkthrough: Bank of Scotland reads as the lender; it is a Scottish bank of earth.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional use: brae is the Scots word for a hillside or steep bank.

entries.clue: Contact that woman about checking account (5)

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, as in about-face, so HER becomes REH
checking something holds it back, so REH holds AC in its grip

annotation.surface: Getting in touch with a woman about her checking account.
annotation.walkthrough: Checking account suggests banking; checking here means restraining.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to get hold of someone by phone or letter is to get through to them.

entries.clue: Sociable former leftie welcoming vicar from down under (9)

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them in, so TROT takes the vicar inside
in a down clue, reading from under means reading from the bottom up

annotation.surface: A friendly ex-Trotskyist hosting a vicar from Australia.
annotation.walkthrough: From down under suggests Australia; in a down clue it means upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: outgoing people who love company are sociable.

entries.clue: This won’t end well, as undertaker might put it (3,4,7)

blocks.note: the idiom warning someone that the bad consequences are theirs
taken literally, what an undertaker could say to a client

annotation.surface: A warning that things will go badly, in an undertaker's phrasing.
annotation.walkthrough: The idiom warns someone that the consequences are theirs; an undertaker could say it literally.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase tells someone their rash choice will rebound on them, and it is also literally an undertaker's line.

entries.clue: Naval officer celebrated defending west following hostilities (4-3)

indicators.note: to defend something is to surround and protect it, so STAR closes round W

blocks.note: a star is celebrated, split round W

annotation.surface: A famous naval officer holding the western front after the fighting.
annotation.walkthrough: Celebrated reads as a verb of partying; it is the adjective famous.
annotation.definitionFit: Latin prefix: post means after, so the word names the period once fighting has ended.

entries.clue: Constituent’s got teeth into first minor role (3,4)

indicators.note: first says which word comes at the front, so BIT goes before PART

blocks.note: a part is a constituent; the ’s is 'has'

annotation.surface: A voter who has sunk their teeth into a small first job.
annotation.walkthrough: Constituent reads as a voter; it is a component, and constituent’s means constituent has.
annotation.definitionFit: Theatre term: a small acting part with few lines.

entries.clue: Time to replace female in flawed investigative role (9)

indicators.note: to replace something is to take its place, so T takes the place of F

annotation.surface: A plea to recast a poorly written female detective part.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures casting a TV role; the swap is one letter inside a word meaning flawed.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the part in a whodunit whose job is to investigate.

entries.clue: Lout rounds on upper-class Brit (5)

indicators.note: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B, so the rounds come after the Brit

blocks.note: a yah is a posh Brit, from their way of saying yes

annotation.surface: A thug going for a posh British man.
annotation.walkthrough: Rounds on reads as attacks, the lout turning on the toff; it is a placement instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Literary origin: Swift's brutish Yahoos in Gulliver's Travels gave the word for a coarse lout.

entries.clue: Man of the cloth shot at table, I hear (5)

indicators.note: what I hear is the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: a cannon is a billiards shot striking two balls

annotation.surface: A priest playing a shot at the billiard table.
annotation.walkthrough: The table is a billiards or snooker table, where a cannon is a shot hitting two balls in turn.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a cathedral clergyman is one kind of man of the cloth.

entries.clue: Falls that may affect your vision? (9)

annotation.surface: A question whether waterfalls can spoil your view.
annotation.walkthrough: Falls reads as tumbles; it is waterfalls.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: great waterfalls, and the eye condition that clouds the lens.

entries.clue: Hangers-on left without whiskey today (9)

indicators.note: without means lacking, so WENT does without its W

blocks.note: whiskey is W in the phonetic alphabet, removed

annotation.surface: Groupies going home dry these days.
annotation.walkthrough: Whiskey is the NATO alphabet's W, not a drink.
annotation.definitionFit: Collective noun: the followers around a celebrity, the hangers-on.

entries.clue: Biography of a setter? It’s not much fun (1,4,4)

blocks.note: a setter is a gun dog, and its biography is its life
the idiom for a miserable existence

annotation.surface: A crossword setter's life story, dismissed as dull.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter is the dog breed, not the crossword compiler.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a wretched, put-upon existence, and literally the life of a dog such as a setter.

entries.clue: Election official hosting party briefly — she’s off to foreign parts (9)

definitions.note: The definition is a clause describing the answer: a person heading abroad.

indicators.note: a host has guests inside the house, so TELLER holds the party
said briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a teller counts votes, split round RAV

annotation.surface: A vote counter throwing a quick party before leaving the country.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash splits wordplay from a definition that is a whole clause, describing the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Description: someone going abroad is making a journey.

entries.clue: Raised current trouble with offspring’s affair (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted up means written upwards

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A parent angry about a child's romance.
annotation.walkthrough: Raised sounds like anger at the affair; it only lifts the first two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a secret romantic relationship, an affair.

entries.clue: It’s dependent on soldier getting hold of £1 (7)

indicators.note: to get hold of something is to grasp it, so RE and ANT close round LI

blocks.note: L for pound, I for one

annotation.surface: A soldier's pay packet: surviving on a single pound.
annotation.walkthrough: Dependent on looks like one phrase; on belongs to the wordplay as RE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: leaning on something else for support.

entries.clue: Ignore fool on vacation abroad (5)

indicators.note: a vacated place has been emptied, so fool loses its middle

annotation.surface: Advice to pay no attention to an idiot on holiday overseas.
annotation.walkthrough: On vacation means a holiday; here it empties fool.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to disregard a rule openly and with contempt.

entries.clue: Earlier I fled, carrying weapon (5)

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it inside, as these words hold the answer

annotation.surface: A confession of escaping while armed.
annotation.walkthrough: Carrying reads as bearing arms, which suits the surface, but it is the hiding instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a long-barrelled gun is one kind of weapon.

entries.clue: Enemy capturing retreating king’s army (5)

indicators.note: to capture is to take prisoner and hold, so FOE holds RC inside
a retreating army goes backwards, so CR is written backwards

blocks.note: a foe is an enemy, split round RC

annotation.surface: An enemy seizing a defeated king's troops.
annotation.walkthrough: CR stands for Carolus Rex, King Charles.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a body of troops, as in armed forces.

entries.clue: Pull Danes out completely (3,4,2)

indicators.note: out can mean out of order or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An order to haul the Danes out entirely.
annotation.walkthrough: Out completely looks like one phrase; out is the anagram signal and completely stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to beat someone all ends up is to beat them thoroughly.

entries.clue: Wine producer’s drink? There’s nothing in it (5)

indicators.note: something in it sits inside it, so O sits inside the drink

annotation.surface: A vintner's glass turns out to be empty.
annotation.walkthrough: The producer is the grape, not the winemaker.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword stretch: the Pinot grape varieties produce wines such as Pinot Noir.

entries.clue: Accra poorly placed as capital (7)

indicators.note: letters poorly placed are in the wrong positions and need moving

annotation.surface: A verdict that Accra is badly sited to be a capital.
annotation.walkthrough: Accra, capital of Ghana, is only fodder; the answer is another capital.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Venezuelan seat of government is one capital city.

entries.clue: A right lot of wets reportedly in charge (7)

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a spelling that sounds like rain

blocks.note: rain is a lot of wet

annotation.surface: A bunch of feeble moderates running things.
annotation.walkthrough: Wets are weak Tory moderates in British politics; here the wet stuff is rain. In charge looks like one phrase, but in is a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal sense: to call someone before a court to answer a formal accusation.

entries.clue: Goes back to well (4)

indicators.note: going back means going the reverse way, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: goes = pees, as in goes to the toilet

annotation.walkthrough: Well is the verb, as in tears welling up.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb sense: liquid that wells up oozes slowly out.

entries.clue: Final part of scene omitted from terribly sentimental episode (10)

indicators.note: the final part of a word is its last letter
something omitted is left out, so that letter leaves the word
something done terribly is done badly, so the remaining letters come out jumbled

annotation.surface: Cutting the last bit of a scene from a mawkish soap episode.
annotation.walkthrough: SENTIMENTAL has two Es; losing either leaves the same ten letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: one part of a serial broadcast or published in parts.
